Variants.Content: The Highgarden outer wall refers to the urban hinterland formed around the Highgarden city walls, gardens, mills, farmsteads and the Mander River crossing. Highgarden's power does not end with the lord's hall in the castle: spices, bread, wine, horses, flowers, maesters and visiting vassals all need the support of surrounding lands and waterways. The Tyrell family built their reputation on roses and generosity, but the residents of the outer lands were more concerned with market prices, taxes, irrigation, and keeping the city gates open on time. Once a banquet is held or an army is summoned to Highgarden, the nearby roads will immediately become busy; once the food route is blocked, the prosperity will quickly become fragile.

Entry Outer Ward of Highgarden Local families also relied on grain, wine, orchards, pastures, and markets along the Mander River; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Outer Ward of Highgarden If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Outer Ward of Highgarden A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Outer Ward of Highgarden They care about grain, wine, orchards, pastures and markets along the Mander River. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
